section_summary: This section consists of State Department correspondence, military permit action slips, travel applications, and diplomatic notes from November 1949 regarding foreign nationals and commercial representatives seeking entry or transit permits for occupied Japan. The cases involve commercial entrants in textiles, pearls, and general merchandise, official missions such as Thai representatives retrieving gold and a Costa Rican trade envoy, as well as Irish Catholic missionary priests transiting to Korea and dependents seeking to join relatives. Prominent administrative matters handled by the Division of Protective Services and the Pacific Military Permit Branch include verifying valid passports, entry documentation for third countries, and coordinating Theater clearances with the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP).
